channel.title: Tech Watch
channel.description: AI, security and architecture news, summarized.

item.title: OpenSSH flaw lets attackers log into password-disabled Linux accounts
item.description: A newly disclosed OpenSSH flaw lets attackers log into password-disabled Alpine and other musl-based Linux accounts by submitting an oversized password.

item.title: Alpine Linux Security Advisory: OpenSSH-server password authentication bypass
item.description: Alpine Linux published a security advisory for an OpenSSH server password authentication bypass vulnerability.

item.title: AI Agents Got Root on Linux via 948 Kernel Flaws in OpenAI Research
item.description: An unreleased OpenAI cyber model found and exploited 948 Linux kernel privilege-escalation bugs for about $1.2 million.

item.title: GitHub to Block pull_request_target Workflows by Default Starting December 2
item.description: GitHub will block pull_request_target workflows by default starting December 2 as an Actions security hardening measure.

item.title: OpenSSH Issues Emergency Fix for Flaw Letting Long Passwords Bypass SSH Auth on Alpine Linux
item.description: OpenSSH released 10.6p2 to fix a critical flaw letting 257-1024 byte passwords bypass SSH auth on some Alpine Linux servers; Alpine issued fixed packages.

item.title: Introducing AWS account access manager: IAM role flexibility with centralized workforce access
item.description: AWS introduced IAM account access manager, combining IAM role flexibility with IAM Identity Center federation and user-level visibility for workforce access.

item.title: Hackers backdoor Linux servers using trojanized CWP web server
item.description: CWPdoor Linux malware is distributed through a trojanized version of cwpsrv, the web server behind the Control Web Panel management interface.

item.title: DigiCert data breach exposes customer information, identity documents
item.description: DigiCert reported a breach after a server migration exposed an internal system to the internet, leaking customer information and identity documents.

item.title: Zyxel fixes zero-day exploited to hack nearly 1,000 network switches
item.description: Zyxel patched a zero-day in GS1900 switches that attackers exploited to compromise nearly 1,000 devices and steal configs and credentials.

item.title: Critical Rails Flaw Lets Attackers Write Server Files via Crafted ImageMagick Uploads
item.description: A critical Rails Active Storage flaw lets unauthenticated attackers write arbitrary server files via crafted ImageMagick uploads; fixed in 8.1.4.1 and 8.0.5.2.

item.title: Xen Hypervisor Flaws Let One Malicious VM Read and Write Any Other VM's Memory
item.description: Two Xen flaws let a malicious guest VM read and write other VMs' memory, including dom0; patches are out with no known mitigation.

item.title: A thousand fewer paths to root
item.description: OpenAI built an autonomous pipeline that found, validated and patched 948 Linux kernel local privilege-escalation vulnerabilities.

item.title: DreamHost confirms data breach exposed FTP logins and webmail sessions
item.description: DreamHost disclosed a breach exposing customer FTP/SFTP credentials and webmail sessions after two months of access.

item.title: Debian and Ubuntu APT Flaw Lets MitM Attackers Swap Verified Packages and Run Code as Root
item.description: A Debian and Ubuntu APT flaw lets attackers who can modify downloads swap verified packages and run code as root.

item.title: APT29-Linked Hackers Hijack Web Analytics Script to Deliver iOS and Android Exploits
item.description: APT29 is suspected of a watering hole campaign using a compromised Ukrainian analytics script to deliver iOS and Android exploits.

item.title: China-Aligned Hackers Hijack Sogou Input Method DNS Requests to Deploy DarkVigil Backdoor
item.description: A China-aligned group hijacked DNS requests from Windows Sogou Input Method to deploy the DarkVigil backdoor in a surveillance campaign.

item.title: Red Hat Patches 9.8-Rated Linux TCP RCE Flaw While Ubuntu Releases Fixes for Testing
item.description: Red Hat released kernel fixes for a 9.8-rated remote unauthenticated use-after-free RCE in Linux IPv4 TCP (CVE-2026-98432); Ubuntu fixes remain in opt-in testing.

item.title: Attackers Exploit Critical Siemens IoT2050 Flaw to Plant Remote Command Backdoors
item.description: VulnCheck reports active exploitation of a CVSS 10.0 missing-authentication flaw (CVE-2026-58115) in Siemens SIMATIC IoT2050 Advanced devices allowing unauthenticated remote code execution.

item.title: Chainstack Reports Production Systems Breach Exposing Customer Data and Password Hashes
item.description: Chainstack disclosed a breach of parts of its infrastructure exposing customer data and password hashes, tied to an AI-powered campaign.

item.title: Binance Reveals How Fake Job Interviews and AI Tool Abuse Led to $6.43 Billion Theft
item.description: Binance said a $6.43 billion theft involved a tampered Homebrew install and fake job-interview social engineering targeting two engineers.

item.title: Barracuda Flaws Could Be Chained to Bypass Authorization and Gain Root Access
item.description: Barracuda disclosed two flaws that can be chained to bypass authorization and gain root, including a 9.3-rated pre-auth bypass.

item.title: Google Warns LLMjacking Attacks Are Costing Some Enterprises Up to $1 Million in Cloud Charges
item.description: Google warned that LLMjacking, hijacking enterprise LLM access via stolen keys, is costing some enterprises up to $1 million in cloud charges.

item.title: cPGuard Update Channel Hijacked to Backdoor Linux Servers and Collect Password Hashes
item.description: Attackers hijacked the cPGuard update channel to send a backdoor script to about 2,950 Linux servers and collect password hashes.

item.title: Hackers Exploit BTCPay Server Flaw to Steal Bitcoin and Litecoin From Hot Wallets
item.description: BTCPay Server urged users to upgrade after Bitcoin and Litecoin were stolen from hot wallets on instances running version 2.4.1 or earlier.

item.title: Shutting the Door on the XCPE Botnet
item.description: Google and partners dismantled the XCPE backdoor botnet of over 1.3 million set-top boxes, attributed to manufacturer Videostrong for ad fraud.

item.title: Google and Meta Open-Source TorchTPU to Bring Native PyTorch Support to Google TPUs
item.description: Google and Meta open-sourced TorchTPU, a native PyTorch backend for Google TPUs supporting eager and compiled execution and distributed computing with minimal code changes.

item.title: Scaling Git at OpenAI
item.description: OpenAI built Pando, a Git-compatible backend, to handle repository scale driven by Codex-assisted development.

item.title: Google Disrupts 1.3 Million-Device Android Botnet, Says TV Box Maker Sold Criminal Access
item.description: Google took down a 1.3 million-device Android TV box botnet and said manufacturer Videostrong intentionally shipped a backdoor and sold access to criminals.

item.title: Critical Langflow Flaws Could Let Unauthenticated Attackers Run Code on Servers
item.description: IBM disclosed two critical Langflow flaws allowing unauthenticated auth bypass and remote code execution in versions 1.0.0 through 1.12.8; only 1.13.0 fixes them.

item.title: Attackers Pose as IT Support on Microsoft Teams, Abuse AD CS to Steal Company Data
item.description: Microsoft reported intrusions where attackers posed as IT support on Teams, took remote control of PCs, then abused insecure AD CS settings to obtain privileged certificates.

item.title: Build efficient agents with knowledge distillation on Amazon SageMaker AI
item.description: AWS shows sequence-level knowledge distillation to transfer frontier model agentic behavior into smaller, cheaper student models on SageMaker AI.

item.title: Beyond DKIM key rotation: understanding email replay attacks
item.description: AWS explains email replay attacks that pass DKIM verification from unrecognized IPs and why key rotation alone does not stop them.

item.title: CVSS 10.0 LXD, MicroCloud Flaw Lets Attackers Impersonate Trusted Clients Without a Private Key
item.description: A CVSS 10.0 flaw in Canonical LXD and MicroCloud let attackers impersonate trusted clients without their private key via the HTTPS API.

item.title: Hackers Steal About $2.7 Million From Polymarket Traders via Hijacked DebugBear Script
item.description: Malicious code replacing a third-party DebugBear script on Polymarket sold traders' positions and moved about $2.7 million; Polymarket is refunding 726 wallets.

item.title: Quoting Kyle Kingsbury
item.description: Jepsen's Kyle Kingsbury argues LLM use erodes trust in documentation and software, making mature-system signals easier to counterfeit.

item.title: FBI Links North Korea's TraderTraitor to Record $6.43 Billion Binance Crypto Heist
item.description: The FBI attributed the theft of over $6 billion in virtual assets from Binance to North Korea's TraderTraitor group.

item.title: Attackers Chain Three Ivanti Connect Secure Flaws to Gain Unauthenticated Root Access
item.description: CISA added two Ivanti Connect Secure flaws to its KEV catalog after attackers chained three vulnerabilities to gain unauthenticated root access.

item.title: Inside a malicious Claude Code-branded extension and its persistent SSH backdoor
item.description: Microsoft documents a malicious Claude Code-branded extension that installs a persistent SSH backdoor, with detection and remediation guidance.

item.title: How We Took Over ChatGPT Accounts
item.description: Parameter Labs documented a complex exploit chain that took over ChatGPT accounts via the sandboxed HTML preview artifacts feature.

item.title: A Shared ChatGPT Link Could Run Attacker Code in Your Session and Read Private Chats
item.description: Researchers found a malicious ChatGPT share link could execute attacker code in a logged-in session and read private chats; OpenAI fixed it in eight days.

item.title: From help desk impersonation to AD CS abuse: Investigating ESC1 and ESC8 intrusion paths
item.description: Microsoft details an intrusion chain from help desk impersonation to AD CS abuse via ESC1 and ESC8 certificate templates.

item.title: Managing Amazon Bedrock costs end to end: A playbook for FinOps and platform teams
item.description: AWS publishes a five-stage FinOps playbook for attributing, observing, budgeting and optimizing Amazon Bedrock costs.

item.title: 4 real? Tracking exploitation and patching of eMudhra’s weak keys
item.description: Cloudflare patched weak eMudhra certificate keys, tracked exploitation attempts, and found much of the Internet still exposed.

item.title: Cloudflare services for private origins is now generally available
item.description: Cloudflare made private-origin services generally available, applying WAF, bot management, caching and Workers to private backends.

item.title: Making it easier for websites to express AI training preferences
item.description: OpenAI said it will honor a shared robots.txt signal letting websites express AI training preferences to participating providers.

item.title: Cursor Removes Malicious Claude Code 2.1.313 Extension From Its Marketplace
item.description: Cursor removed a malicious Claude Code 2.1.313 extension from its marketplace after Socket examined registry records and distribution claims.

item.title: GitLab Patch Release and Security Update: 19.5.3, 19.4.5, 19.3.7, 19.2.10, 19.1.10, 19.0.11, 18.11.14
item.description: GitLab released patch versions for CE and EE addressing CVE-2026-111943 plus GitLab Runner and AI Gateway updates.

item.title: Searchjacked: Hidden Browser Extensions Hijack Searches for 13 Million Users
item.description: 319 browser extensions installed by 13.4 million users hijack searches, capture queries and collect referral payments from Yahoo and Bing.

item.title: Cloudflare DDoS Threat Report 2026 Q3: More swarms, fewer giants
item.description: Cloudflare's Q3 2026 DDoS report shows over 8,200 attacks per hour, with shorter high-frequency strikes replacing large ones.

item.title: The boundary problem in agentic AI is a platform problem
item.description: A CNCF post argues that agentic AI risk is bounded by what an agent's tools permit, making it a platform concern.
